**Every finding and every actionable lead is closed**, and the one host-level
item is now done too — see the rotation below. One lead is deliberately left
alone.

### Database password — ROTATED 2026-09-09

The old value was exposed twice: committed to this repo at `522774f` (private,
but permanent in history), and later a fragment of it landed in a session
transcript via a `psql` error. Rotated the same day.

Verified by proving the **old** password no longer authenticates, rather than by
watching the new one work — a backend that never reconnected would also report
healthy, so the negative test is the one that carries information:

```
FATAL:  password authentication failed for user "makr_ge"
```

with `/health` returning `{"status":"ok","database":"up"}` and the public site
answering 200 on `/public/stats`. The compose backup holding the old value was
deleted afterwards.

**The rotation corrected a documentation error worth knowing about.**
`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` said the secret lived in `/opt/ge/.env`. That path has
never existed. GE is managed by the Plesk Docker extension, so `DATABASE_URL`
and `JWT_SECRET` sit inline in
`/opt/psa/var/modules/docker/stacks/ge/compose.yaml`. Anyone following the doc
during an incident would have searched the wrong filesystem. The doc now says
where the value is and, more usefully, how to ask the container instead of
trusting a written path.

Procedure, verification commands and the URL-encoding trap are recorded under
"Rotating the database password" in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

### `:3100` exposure — CHECKED 2026-09-09, not exposed

The review could not probe this and correctly refused to guess. Answered from
both sides:

- **On the host:** `iptables -P INPUT DROP`, 24 ACCEPT rules, none covering 3100
  (nearest is `49152:65535`). firewalld not running, ufw inactive.
- **From outside:** unreachable from two independent machines on two networks,
  each with `:443` as a control so a false negative from a broken path would
  show up. nginx reaches the app at `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3100`.

**Still worth hardening, and not done.** The container runs `network_mode: host`
and the app listens on `*:3100` — every interface — where `ge-frontend` binds
`127.0.0.1:8081`. It is safe today by ONE mechanism: the iptables default
policy. One broad ACCEPT rule, or a Plesk firewall regeneration, and the game's
API is on the public internet with no TLS and no nginx in front of it.
`app.listen(port, '127.0.0.1')` would cost nothing — nginx already reaches it on
loopback — and would make it two independent mechanisms instead of one. Deploy
risk is real (bind it wrong and the site 502s), so it wants building and booting
locally first, the way the non-root image change was.

### Leads reassessed after Part A

| Lead | Now |
|---|---|
| One socket exhausting the DB pool by flooding commands | **Largely closed** by Part A — a socket can have one command in flight. Message-level flooding (CPU, memory) is untouched. |
| `sen` as an unthrottled broadcast primitive | **FIXED (v0.12.0)** — rolling window, 5 sends per 5s per pilot, refusals not counted against the sender; `chat-throttle.spec.ts` (6) + `sen-throttle.spec.ts` (4). Port-original: canon throttles `send` not at all. |
| Unlimited concurrent sockets per account | **FIXED (v0.12.0)** — 4 per account, evicting the OLDEST so a player's own stale tabs can never lock them out; `socket-cap-per-account.spec.ts` (5). |
| Backend container runs as root | **FIXED (v0.12.0)** — `USER node`, with `--chown=node:node` on the runtime COPYs. Verified by building and booting the image, not by reading it: Prisma refuses to run unless it can write to `@prisma/engines`, so the first attempt would have failed `migrate deploy` and taken the game down. `dockerfile-nonroot.spec.ts` (3) guards the directives. |
| Cargo tonnage from a stale snapshot | **Closed in practice** — the same-socket race is gone with Part A, and ship item counts can no longer go negative, which was what manufactured phantom capacity. |
| `/auth/register` email enumeration | **Won't fix for the beta, deliberately** — and now with a condition attached. A signup form that will not say "already registered" is a worse product, and the address is the login identifier. Re-derived 2026-09-09: the message cannot be fixed on its own, because registration issues a usable session immediately, so the leak survives as a two-request oracle. Real fix = email verification + neutral responses on register/resend/reset + queued mail for constant time. Scheduled for before going public; see the backlog in `docs/PROGRESS.md`. |

**Both parts are done.** Part B made the invariants Postgres's job:
every cash debit re-checks the balance in the same statement that spends it, and
`depositToPlanet` takes the cargo from the hull inside the planet lock the way
`sell()` always did. That holds regardless of scheduling, of two sockets on one
account, or of a tick interleaving with a command.

Part A — serializing command dispatch per socket (§5 item 1) — followed in
v0.11.0 as a separate change so any latency effect would be attributable. Cost
measured rather than assumed: every combat and navigation command makes zero
database calls, so the queue adds one microtask and a pilot can only wait behind
a trade or admin verb, which needs orbit. The ticks are deliberately outside the
queue, so the world does not pause while a command is queued.

Both fixes were verified in both directions: the two new specs fail against the
unfixed code (5 of 8 cases) and pass against it. They run on a REAL Postgres,
because the race lives in the gap between a read and a write that a mocked
client does not have.

The `COMBAT_SHIP_DESTROYED` lead was verified and turned out real: the handler
spread the whole internal event into a galaxy-wide emit, publishing every kill's
exact sector, both internal account keys, the destroyed hull's cargo and the
victim's socket disconnect reason. The client renders four fields; it now
receives four.

The remaining unconfirmed leads are unchanged and still unverified, except the
two that M4 subsumed. Of them, `/auth/register`'s EMAIL_TAKEN-vs-201
enumeration is real but is a deliberate trade — a signup form that will not say
"that address is already registered" is a worse product for a private-beta game,
and the address is already the login identifier. Not changed; noted so it is not
re-raised.


# Security Review — Galactic Empire Reborn

**Date:** 2026-09-09 · **Scope:** `backend/`, `frontend/`, deployment config. `reference/` excluded by design.

---

## 1. Verdict

The security fundamentals are genuinely solid: JWT handling fails closed, authorization on every command handler resolves the actor from the verified token rather than from client input, all SQL is parameterised, the debug and admin gates are double fail-closed, and the frontend has no XSS surface at all. What is weak is *concurrency and scoping inside the game layer* — commands are dispatched without awaiting or serializing per socket, so every read-then-await-then-write in the economy is racable by one client, and two broadcast paths hand out player positions the visibility design exists to withhold.

No critical or high finding survived verification. Six mediums, all fixable in an afternoon.

---

## 2. Confirmed findings

### M1. Credit-balance TOCTOU across every purchase handler, amplified by a debt-forgiving clamp

**`backend/src/game/commands/handlers/buy.handler.ts:88-92` (read), `:147-149` (debit), `:93-98` (clamp)**

`buy` reads cash with a bare `findUnique`, awaits the planet transaction, then applies an unconditional `decrement`. Nothing serializes commands from one socket: `game.gateway.ts:917-931` fires `commandRouter.dispatch` and only `.then()`s the promise — no per-socket queue, no rate limit (grepped `gateway/` and `command-router.service.ts` for queue/mutex/throttle: nothing). `PlanetStateService.runSerialized` (`planet-state.service.ts:188-196`) keys the lock on the **planet**, so the user row never enters the critical section.

**Attack.** In orbit at Zygor with C credits, from devtools:
```js
for (let i=0;i<20;i++) socket.emit('command',{input:'buy 100 missiles'})
```
The first `await` inside `handle()` is the `findUnique`, so all twenty packets reach it before any resolves; all twenty read cash = C, all twenty pass `totalCost > buyerCash` (`planet-trade.ts:131`), all twenty commit cargo. Cash is now ≈ −19C. Then type `buy 1 food`: lines 93-98 see the negative balance and write `cash: 0n`, cancelling the debt. `sell` the goods back (`sell.handler.ts:71-75` credits with an atomic `increment`) and repeat. Unbounded.

Note the clamp itself is **canon** — `reference/ge-source/GECMDS.C:4205-4207` does exactly this, and canon was safe because MajorBBS serialized one command per user. The defect is the missing serialization, not the clamp.

Same shape in `new-ship.handler.ts:228-232` / `:503-509` (which also reads the `noships` fleet cap outside any lock), `new-ship.handler.ts:371`, and `maintenance.service.ts:100,120` — so `new ship 5` and `new phaser 8` fired together both go through on one balance. Cargo capacity at `buy.handler.ts:79-84` is computed pre-await too, so concurrent buys also overfill the hold.

**Fix.** Make the check and the debit one statement:
```ts
const { count } = await prisma.user.updateMany({
  where: { userid, cash: { gte: totalCost } },
  data: { cash: { decrement: totalCost } },
});
if (count === 0) return INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS;
```
…and commit goods only after it succeeds. Independently, chain each `dispatch` onto a per-client promise in the gateway so two handlers for one player are never in flight together — that closes the entire class in one change. Keep the canon clamp, but it should become unreachable.

---

### M2. `transfer down` duplicates items onto a planet against a hull that can be discarded

**`backend/src/game/commands/handlers/transfer.handler.ts:62-65` (check), `:76` (await), `:85-87` (decrement)**

The cargo-sufficiency check is synchronous, the deposit is awaited, and the ship is debited afterwards. `depositToPlanet` (`planet-state.service.ts:666-684`) runs inside the per-planet lock but does `state.items[itemIndex].qty += qty` at `:676` with **no re-read of the source hull** — the inverse of `PlanetStateService.sell` (`:415-441`), which deliberately re-reads and decrements the seller's cargo *inside* the lock and says so in its JSDoc. `ShipStateService.mutate` (`ship-state.service.ts:240-250`) applies mutations with no clamp; there is no `Math.max(0, …)` on item counts anywhere in `game/ship/`.

**Attack.** Land on any planet carrying q gold. Fire `tra down q gold` ten times in one batch — all ten pass line 62 against the same snapshot, the planet gains 10q, the ship holds −9q. The check-to-mutate window spans a full Postgres round-trip, so no precise timing is needed. Buy a fresh hull with `new ship` (or let the negative one be destroyed) — the debt dies with the hull, the 10q on the planet does not. `tra up` in q-sized lots and `sell` at Zygor at 1,000 credits each (`constants/items.ts:92`). Net creation of 9q gold per cycle.

Secondary: `buy.handler.ts:81-86` and `transfer.handler.ts:117-121` both compute used tonnage as a plain sum over `items`, so a −1,000,000 gold balance (0.5 t each) manufactures 500,000 tons of phantom cargo capacity.

**Fix.** Pass `(userid, shipno, itemIndex, qty)` into `depositToPlanet` and do the ship re-read, re-check and decrement inside `runSerialized` — copy `sell()` exactly. Reject any mutation that would take a ship item below zero. Note `depositToPlanet` has no owner check at all; that part is deliberate per canon `TRANSOPT`, so leave it.

---

### M3. Unscoped galaxy-wide `player.snapshot` — any player can dump every pilot's exact sector on demand

**`backend/src/gateway/game.gateway.ts:2524-2525`**

```ts
if (broadcast.event === 'player.snapshot') {
  this.server.emit('player.snapshot', { players: this.registry.list() });
```
`ConnectedShipsRegistry.list()` (`connected-ships.registry.ts:86-101`) unconditionally fills `sector: { x: Math.floor(ship.xcoord), y: Math.floor(ship.ycoord) }` for every registered ship — its own doc comment says `scopePlayers()` is what blanks it. `scopePlayers` has exactly **one** call site, `game.gateway.ts:384` (the connect/welcome path). This branch has none. The scoping work in 51c2b9c missed `processBroadcasts`.

**Attack.** Log in as any ordinary player. Type `ren Foo1`, then `ren Foo2`, alternating. Each successful rename returns the `__player_snapshot__` sentinel (`rename.handler.ts:81-86`; a byte-identical name short-circuits at `:52-57`, hence the alternation) and the gateway broadcasts the full unscoped roster to every socket including the attacker's: `{shipId, name, sector:{x,y}, shipClass}` for every connected pilot, cloaked ships included, at unlimited range, with no scan notice to targets. `RenameService.rename` (`rename.service.ts:34-88`) has no gold cost, no cooldown and no per-session limit. Poll it every few seconds for a live position tracker of the whole roster — pick the richest target off `ros`, watch their sector, intercept. All five `tea` subcommands fire the same sentinel (`tea.handler.ts:143,182,229,270,303`), so a player who never renames leaks everyone's position to everyone whenever they touch a team command.

This is exactly the class of leak the v0.7.1–v0.8.1 `who`/`dat`/`sca` fixes closed, on a path they missed. `sector` is `Math.floor` of the raw coordinate — a 1-unit cell in a ±100 universe, i.e. a precise fix, not a coarse region. Client-side filtering is no defence; `player-visibility.ts:12-20` already says the gate has to sit on the wire.

**Fix.** The payload differs per recipient, so the broadcast must be a per-socket fan-out: walk `server.sockets.sockets`, resolve each viewer's ship from `sock.data.userid`/`sock.data.activeShipNo`, and emit `scopePlayers(this.registry.list(), viewerSector)` — the same shape `emitScopedSnapshot` already builds. If the intent is only "a name changed", emit a `{shipId, name}` delta instead of a roster.

---

### M4. `sector:join` lets any authenticated player subscribe to every sector room

**`backend/src/gateway/game.gateway.ts:1154-1178`**

The only gate is `client.data.userid && this.registry.isBound(client.id)` — "are you a bound player", never "is this your sector". `validateCoord` (`:2595-2617`) checks only integer type and ±UNIVMAX bounds, so all 201×201 rooms are reachable, then `client.join('sector:x:y')` runs unconditionally.

**Attack.** Board a ship normally, then loop `socket.emit('sector:join',{x,y})` across the whole grid (40,401 rooms). `handleSectorTransition` at `:2308-2312` emits `player.sector { updates: [{ shipId, sector: toSector }] }` **with explicit coordinates in the payload** to the destination sector room, for every ship that isn't `GESTAT_AUTO` (`transition-visibility.ts:22`) — i.e. every human. Named arrival/departure lines at `:692-698` and `:715-721` add to it. Result: a live galaxy-wide position tracker. Nothing ever removes the joins — the only `.leave(` call sites are `:1202` (`sector:leave`) and `:2333` (the mover's own from-sector); rooms clear only on disconnect. There is no room cap and no rate limit, so the join loop is also an unbounded per-socket allocation.

Two corrections to note if you're triaging: `sector:ship-entered`/`ship-left` (`:2367-2374`) and `BEACON_EVENT` (`:2399`) carry **no** coordinates, and Socket.io does not tell a client which room delivered an event — so those alone leak nothing. `player.sector` is the actual channel.

**Fix.** Delete the handler. `grep` shows `sector:join`/`sector:leave` appear only in `game.gateway.ts` — the frontend never emits them, and ships are placed in rooms server-side by `joinPlayerRooms`. It is unused legacy surface. If you keep it, derive x/y from `shipStateService.get(client.data.userid, client.data.activeShipNo)` and ignore the payload entirely.

---

### M5. Auth throttling keys on the proxy's IP — one host can lock everyone out of login and registration

**`backend/src/main.ts:7-14`** (no `app.set('trust proxy', …)`) · **`backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:38`** (`ttl: 60_000, limit: 10`)

`@nestjs/throttler` 5.2.0's default tracker is `req.ip` (`throttler.guard.js:122-124`). Express's `trust proxy` defaults to false and nothing sets it; `grep -rn "trust proxy|getTracker" backend/src` returns nothing and there is no `ThrottlerGuard` subclass. Behind the documented nginx → `127.0.0.1:3000` hop (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:116-123`), `req.ip` is the loopback proxy address for every internet caller. No nginx-level `limit_req` compensates.

`generateKey` hashes `${Class}-${handler}-${name}-${tracker}`, so the three auth routes get separate buckets — but each bucket's tracker is that one constant IP, shared by the whole internet.

**Attack.** Send ~11 `POST /auth/login` per 60s from one host with a bogus email. `ThrottlerStorageService.increment` (`throttler.service.js:31-46`) counts requests it is about to reject, and only decrements 60s after recording, so the bucket stays saturated indefinitely. Every real visitor gets 429 on login. Repeat on `/auth/register` to block signups. Unauthenticated, one host, negligible cost. Existing players holding a 30-day JWT stay connected — the outage is on new logins and registrations.

The code comments at `auth.module.ts:33-37` and `auth.constants.ts:15-22` both assert the limit is "per caller", and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:137-141` already flags this exact gap as unconfirmed.

**Fix.** `app.set('trust proxy', 'loopback')` in `main.ts` (nginx is on 127.0.0.1). Do **not** trust `X-Forwarded-For` unconditionally — a spoofable tracker is as bad as a shared one.

---

## 3. What was checked and found sound

This is the larger half of the review.

**Authentication.** JWT secret sourcing fails closed in three independent places (`auth.module.ts:22-25`, `jwt.strategy.ts:14-17`, `docker-compose.yml:31` `${JWT_SECRET:?}`) — no placeholder can ship. No algorithm confusion: symmetric string secret, `ignoreExpiration: false`, no `algorithms` override admitting `none`/RS256. bcrypt cost 12; password `MinLength(8)/MaxLength(72)` (72 is bcrypt's truncation point — correct). Login enumeration by timing is closed by the `DUMMY_BCRYPT_HASH` compare, and case-insensitive email matching is done by pre-lowercasing rather than Prisma `mode:'insensitive'` — the comment at `auth.service.ts:199-206` correctly identifies the ILIKE-pattern injection that would otherwise exist. Two-step registration is race-safe: a `username: null` token is refused at the socket (`ws-auth.guard.ts:44-52`) and `chooseUsername` uses `updateMany` with `username: null` in the WHERE (`auth.service.ts:159-178`), so a half-registered account cannot be hijacked. Session eviction is keyed on `shipKey(userid, shipno)` with userid from the verified `sub` (`game.gateway.ts:285-287`), so `SESSION_REPLACED` can only ever evict your own prior socket.

**Authorization.** `isSysop()` runs *before* the subcommand is parsed (`sys.handler.ts:112`), matches `ship.username` against a `GE_SYSOP_USERNAME` allowlist that filters empty entries (`:68-72`, so an unset value grants nobody, not everybody), and returns canon's `"Huh?"` so the toolkit's existence isn't disclosed. Every mutating subcommand acts on `ship.userid`/`ship.shipno` — the caller's own hull — except `sys kill`, which is behind the same gate. Ship selection cannot reach another captain's hull: `pendingShipSelect` is server-built from `findMany({ where: { userid } })`, the reply index is bounds-checked, and the row is re-read with `findFirst({ where: { userid, shipno } })`. Every planet command resolves the planet from `ship.where`/`ship.xcoord`/`ship.ycoord`, never a client-supplied id. Mail `rea`/`del` index into a list already scoped to the caller. Team kick/newpass/newname require the caller's live teamcode plus an exact founder secret, with a blank secret explicitly rejected as a skeleton key; `crypto.randomInt` over a 32-char alphabet; join size cap enforced inside `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. `AdminTokenGuard` 503s when unconfigured (so an empty Bearer cannot match an unset token), requires `Bearer `, and length-checks before a constant-time XOR compare.

**Input handling.** All five raw-SQL sites use Prisma tagged templates with `${}` placeholders; no `$queryRawUnsafe`/`$executeRawUnsafe` anywhere in `backend/src`; no user-controlled identifiers reach SQL. Every numeric command argument is regex-gated before `parseInt` (`validators.ts` `/^-?\d+$/`, `/^\d+$/`, `parseUint32` bounded 0..2³²−1), so `NaN`/`Infinity`/`1e9`/`0x` forms are rejected rather than coerced, and no `BigInt()` receives a non-integer. Socket payloads are type-checked (`command` coerces non-string input to `''` at `:895`; `prompt:reply` validates `Number.isInteger` and bounds). No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `eval`, or `new Function` in the whole frontend — every server string reaches the DOM as a React text child, and no `href`/`src` is ever built from server data. The `sen` chat path was traced end to end: `command-router` splits on `/\s+/` so injected newlines cannot forge log lines, `MAX_MSG_LEN = 200`, and `from` is constrained by `name-validator.ts:7` to `/^[\x21-\x7E]{1,19}$/` — no spaces, so the `[CH] name:` prefix cannot be spoofed. No nested-quantifier regexes on user input. `sen constructor msg` / `fre __proto__ 5` do slip past the `=== undefined` guard in `CHANNEL_MAP`, but the value only indexes the ship's `freq` array — nothing is written to `Object.prototype` and no capability is gained, so it is not reported.

**Deployment.** `GE_DEBUG_ENDPOINTS` is a double fail-closed gate (`debug-endpoints.ts:22-24` — requires an explicit affirmative from `{'1','true','yes','on'}` **and** returns false unconditionally under `NODE_ENV=production`), wired at module-construction time across all five mount points, with `frontend/nginx.conf:31-36` additionally declining to proxy `/debug/`. Postgres publishes no ports at all; production uses the host's native instance over `127.0.0.1`. `git ls-files` finds no tracked `.env`; both Dockerfiles' only build args are `GIT_SHA`/`APP_VERSION`; both `.dockerignore`s exclude `.env*`. CI pins all four third-party actions to commit SHAs, scopes `permissions:` to `contents: read` + `packages: write`, and uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No `enableCors()` in `main.ts`, so the REST API sends no ACAO header; `@WebSocketGateway({ cors: true })` reflects any origin but the handshake carries no cookies (bearer token from localStorage, validated server-side at `:282`), so there is no cross-site hijack path.

**Integrity that is already correct.** `PlanetStateService.sell()` (`:415-441`) is the pattern the other handlers should copy — it re-reads and decrements seller cargo inside the lock, and credits cash with an atomic `increment`. Ship-to-ship `tra <qty> <item> <shipno>` is fully synchronous with no await between check and both mutations, so it cannot be raced, and it gives cargo away rather than taking it. Money and cargo are BigInt end to end, so no overflow path. Midnight is a single `$transaction` gated by a transaction-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock` plus a `MidnightRun` ledger keyed on runDate — concurrent and repeat runs both refused. `withdrawTax` re-validates inside the planet lock. Zygor and Tahanian Station are owned by the `NEUTRAL_ZONE_OWNER` sentinel rather than null, so the "unowned planet" branch does not open the 1,032,000-unit hub restock to free looting. The ship flush clears `dirty` before awaiting and re-raises on failure.

**DoS surface.** `MineRegistry` is hard-capped at `NUMMINES` with `isFull()` gating inserts (`mine.registry.ts:71-73`); projectile slots are fixed-size arrays; `ShipChannelRegistry.release()` scrubs stale references; `scantabMap` is cleared on both `x` and disconnect; `TickService` wraps every subscriber in try/catch plus async `.catch` so a throwing handler cannot stop the loop.

**Deliberately not reported:** cloaked ships being announced on sector entry/exit (canon-faithful, `GEFUNCS.C:709-722` MOVE2/MOVE3 have no cloak test); the 30-day non-revocable JWT (no attacker path without prior token theft); the MAXPLRS seat cap (exhausting it costs credits).

---

## 4. Unconfirmed leads — not verified, do not treat as findings

These hit the verification cap. Each is plausible and each needs its own read before you act.

- **No rate limit or size limit on any WebSocket message** (`game.gateway.ts:873`). One socket can plausibly exhaust the Prisma pool or flood every player. Closely related to M1/M2 — the per-socket serialization fix likely covers most of it. Worth confirming first, since it's the same code change.
- **`sen` on an open hail is an unthrottled galaxy-wide broadcast primitive** (`game.gateway.ts:873`). Payload is capped at 200 chars; the question is cadence.
- **Galaxy-wide `COMBAT_SHIP_DESTROYED` payload may carry the kill's exact sector, the victim's userid and their socket disconnect reason** (`game.gateway.ts:1627`). If true, same disclosure class as M3/M4.
- **Cargo tonnage enforced against a stale snapshot** (`transfer.handler.ts:117`). Almost certainly real — it's the same pre-await computation noted in M2 — but not separately verified.
- **`/auth/register` is an email-enumeration oracle** (`EMAIL_TAKEN` vs 201, `auth.service.ts:105`). Low.
- **Unlimited concurrent sockets per account**, each costing two Prisma queries (`game.gateway.ts:271`). Low.
- **Backend container runs as root and shares the host network namespace in production** (`backend/Dockerfile:20`). Low, and partly a deliberate deployment choice.

**One thing I could not check.** The production host's firewall. The read-only probe over the Plesk connection was blocked by the permission classifier, so I have left it out rather than speculate. Confirm manually that the host-networked backend on `:3100` is **not** reachable from the internet — if it is, it bypasses Plesk's TLS termination *and* the nginx-level decision not to proxy `/debug/`:

```
ss -lnt | grep 3100
iptables -L -n | grep 3100     # or: firewall-cmd --list-all
```

## 5. Do this first

1. **Serialize command dispatch per socket** (`game.gateway.ts:917`) — chain each `dispatch` onto a per-client promise. One change, and it closes M1, M2, the tonnage lead and most of the WS-flood lead at once. Highest value per line changed.
2. **Make the cash debit conditional** (`buy.handler.ts:147`, `new-ship.handler.ts:503`, `maintenance.service.ts:100/120`) — `updateMany` with `cash: { gte: totalCost }`, treat `count === 0` as insufficient funds. Belt to step 1's braces; do it even after serializing, because it makes the invariant enforceable by Postgres rather than by scheduling.
3. **Move the ship-side check and decrement inside `depositToPlanet`'s lock** (`transfer.handler.ts:76`, `planet-state.service.ts:666`) — copy `sell()` verbatim. Add a zero-clamp on ship item counts while you're there; the phantom-tonnage consequence disappears with it.
4. **Delete the `sector:join` / `sector:leave` handlers** (`game.gateway.ts:1154-1210`). Nothing calls them. Five-minute fix, removes M4 entirely.
5. **Scope the `__player_snapshot__` broadcast** (`game.gateway.ts:2524`) — per-socket fan-out through `scopePlayers`, or replace it with a name-only delta. This is the last hole in the v0.7.1–v0.8.1 position-disclosure work.
6. **`app.set('trust proxy', 'loopback')` in `main.ts`**, then verify with a quick 15-request burst from two different source IPs that only the offender gets 429. Also resolve the `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:137-141` note while it's fresh.
7. **Confirm the host firewall** on `:3100`, and rotate the DB password. ~~Both~~ — **both done 2026-09-09**; see the two sections at the top of this file.

Items 1–3 are economy integrity and matter most for a persistent shared world; 4–5 are the disclosure cleanup; 6 is availability.
